objects.description: Codec setup and stream description for a Vorbis logical bitstream (version, channels, sample rate, bitrate hints). Holds an opaque codec_setup pointer used internally by libvorbis.
Holds the DSP analysis/synthesis working state for a specific Vorbis logical bitstream. Contains PCM buffers, block/windowing state, granule tracking, bit metrics, and an internal backend_state.

Represents a single analysis/synthesis block for a Vorbis stream. Holds per-block PCM pointer, bitpacker buffer, window sizes, linkage to a vorbis_dsp_state, local allocation chain, bit metrics, and an internal pointer.
Internal singly linked list node used by vorbis_block for local scratch allocations that can be reaped as a group.
Holds Vorbis comment (metadata) header fields: vendor string and an array of user comments with lengths.
Callback vtable used by vorbisfile to abstract I/O operations (read, seek, close, tell) over arbitrary data sources.
High-level convenience wrapper for opening, decoding, and seeking within Ogg Vorbis files/streams. Manages container parsing, logical links, and decoder state (dsp state and block).
Deprecated encoder bitrate management configuration structure for the original (pre-1.1) window-based rate management interface.
Current encoder bitrate management configuration for bit-reservoir based control; used with vorbis_encode_ctl via OV_ECTL_RATEMANAGE2_GET/SET.

functions.name: vorbis_info_init
functions.description: Initializes a vorbis_info structure for encoder/decoder setup. Call before using the struct with other Vorbis init/setup functions and before any encoding/decoding operation. After use, clear with vorbis_info_clear.
requirements: vi must be a valid, writable pointer
Call this before any encoder or decoder setup that uses vi
Pair with vorbis_info_clear when finished

functions.name: vorbis_info_clear
functions.description: Releases/reset fields inside a vorbis_info previously initialized. Call after encoding/decoding is done to free internal allocations.
requirements: vi must have been initialized with vorbis_info_init (or otherwise valid)
Do not use vi with encoder/decoder after clearing unless reinitialized

functions.name: vorbis_info_blocksize
functions.description: Returns the analysis/synthesis block size for a given mode index (small/large window) from an initialized vorbis_info. Exact meanings depend on codec setup.
requirements: vi must be initialized and configured (e.g., via header parsing or encoder setup)
zo is typically 0 or 1 for small/large windows; other values may be invalid

functions.name: vorbis_comment_init
functions.description: Initializes a vorbis_comment container for attaching metadata (user comments and vendor string).
requirements: vc must be a valid, writable pointer
Pair with vorbis_comment_clear to free resources

functions.name: vorbis_comment_add
functions.description: Appends a raw comment string (typically "TAG=VALUE") to a vorbis_comment.
requirements: vc must be initialized with vorbis_comment_init
comment must be a valid NUL-terminated string
Pair overall comment lifecycle with vorbis_comment_clear

functions.name: vorbis_comment_add_tag
functions.signature: extern void vorbis_comment_add_tag(vorbis_comment *vc, const char *tag, const char *contents);
functions.description: Appends a metadata field to vc given a tag and contents (creates a "TAG=VALUE" entry).
requirements: vc must be initialized with vorbis_comment_init
tag must be a valid NUL-terminated string
contents may be NULL or a valid NUL-terminated string depending on usage (exact behavior not documented here)
Call vorbis_comment_clear to free resources when done

functions.name: vorbis_comment_query
functions.signature: extern char *vorbis_comment_query(vorbis_comment *vc, const char *tag, int count);
functions.description: Returns the Nth string value for a given metadata tag from vc, or NULL if not found. Returned pointer refers to internal storage owned by vc.
requirements: vc must be initialized/populated
tag must be a valid NUL-terminated string
count selects which occurrence (0-based)
Do not free or modify the returned string; it is owned by vc
vc must remain valid while using the returned pointer

functions.name: vorbis_comment_query_count
functions.description: Returns the number of entries present for the given tag in vc.
requirements: vc must be initialized/populated
tag must be a valid NUL-terminated string

functions.name: vorbis_comment_clear
functions.description: Clears and frees internal allocations in a vorbis_comment previously initialized and/or populated.
requirements: vc must have been initialized with vorbis_comment_init
After clearing, do not use the internal pointers; reinitialize before reuse

functions.name: vorbis_block_init
functions.description: Initializes a vorbis_block for analysis/synthesis work tied to an existing vorbis_dsp_state.
requirements: v must be an initialized vorbis_dsp_state for the active stream
vb must be a valid, writable pointer
Call vorbis_block_clear to release resources

functions.name: vorbis_block_clear
functions.description: Clears a vorbis_block previously initialized by vorbis_block_init, releasing internal allocations.
requirements: vb must have been initialized by vorbis_block_init
Do not reuse vb for processing until reinitialized

functions.name: vorbis_dsp_clear
functions.description: Clears decoder/encoder DSP state previously initialized, releasing internal allocations.
requirements: v must have been initialized (e.g., by vorbis_analysis_init or vorbis_synthesis_init)
After clearing, the state is unusable until reinitialized

functions.name: vorbis_granule_time
functions.description: Converts a codec granule position to playback time (seconds) using the sampling rate in the DSP state.
requirements: v must be initialized and associated with a valid vorbis_info containing rate
granulepos is a codec granule position from the stream

functions.name: vorbis_version_string
functions.description: Returns a human-readable libvorbis version string.
requirements: Returned pointer is static storage; do not free or modify

functions.name: vorbis_analysis_init
functions.description: Initializes encoder-side DSP state for analysis/encoding based on a configured vorbis_info.
requirements: vi must be initialized and configured for encoding (e.g., via vorbisenc setup)
v must be a valid, writable pointer
Call vorbis_block_init to create working blocks and vorbis_dsp_clear when done

functions.name: vorbis_commentheader_out
functions.description: Builds the Vorbis comment header packet from vc for stream header emission.
requirements: vc must be initialized/populated (vendor and user comments)
op must be a valid pointer to receive the constructed packet
Typically used during encoder header generation

functions.name: vorbis_analysis_headerout
functions.signature: extern int vorbis_analysis_headerout(vorbis_dsp_state *v, vorbis_comment *vc, ogg_packet *op, ogg_packet *op_comm, ogg_packet *op_code);
functions.description: Generates the three Vorbis header packets (identification, comment, setup) for encoding using the configured DSP state and comments.
requirements: v must be initialized for analysis via vorbis_analysis_init
vc must be initialized/populated
op, op_comm, and op_code must be valid pointers to receive packets
Call before encoding audio packets

functions.name: vorbis_analysis_buffer
functions.description: Returns writeable buffers (per channel) to submit PCM samples for encoding; request vals samples per channel.
requirements: v must be initialized for analysis and not cleared
vals is the number of samples per channel to buffer (non-negative)
Caller must write exactly the returned frame size semantics as required before calling vorbis_analysis_wrote

functions.name: vorbis_analysis_wrote
functions.description: Submits vals samples per channel previously written to the analysis buffer; signal end-of-stream by passing 0 after final data.
requirements: v must be initialized for analysis
vals must match the amount written via vorbis_analysis_buffer for this submission; 0 may signal flush/end
Must be called after writing to buffers returned by vorbis_analysis_buffer

functions.name: vorbis_analysis_blockout
functions.description: Retrieves a prepared analysis block from the encoder DSP for further processing and packetization.
requirements: v must be initialized for analysis and have data submitted
vb must be initialized via vorbis_block_init and writable

functions.name: vorbis_analysis
functions.description: Performs analysis on a prepared block and outputs an encoded packet.
requirements: vb must be initialized and filled by vorbis_analysis_blockout
op must be a valid pointer to receive the encoded packet

functions.name: vorbis_bitrate_addblock
functions.description: Submits an analyzed block to the bitrate management engine for packet formation.
requirements: vb must contain analysis results (from vorbis_analysis) and be valid
Typically followed by vorbis_bitrate_flushpacket to obtain packets

functions.name: vorbis_bitrate_flushpacket
functions.description: Retrieves a packet from the bitrate management engine if available.
requirements: vd must be an initialized encoder DSP state with prior vorbis_bitrate_addblock submissions
op must be a valid pointer to receive a packet

functions.name: vorbis_synthesis_idheader
functions.description: Tests whether an ogg_packet is a Vorbis identification header.
requirements: op must point to a valid packet buffer
Used before headerin to validate streams

functions.name: vorbis_synthesis_headerin
functions.description: Parses Vorbis header packets into vorbis_info and vorbis_comment during decoder setup.
requirements: vi and vc must be initialized (e.g., via vorbis_info_init and vorbis_comment_init)
op must point to a valid header packet (identification, comment, or setup)
Call with all three header packets before initializing the decoder DSP

functions.name: vorbis_synthesis_init
functions.description: Initializes decoder-side DSP state for synthesis/PCM decode from a configured vorbis_info.
requirements: vi must be initialized and populated by header parsing
v must be a valid, writable pointer
Call vorbis_block_init for block workspace and vorbis_dsp_clear when done

functions.name: vorbis_synthesis_restart
functions.description: Resets decoder DSP state for beginning a new logical stream or after a seek without reallocation.
requirements: v must be an initialized synthesis DSP state

functions.name: vorbis_synthesis
functions.description: Decodes a packet into a synthesis block (no PCM return yet).
requirements: vb must be initialized and linked to a synthesis DSP (via vorbis_block_init)
op must point to a valid audio packet

functions.name: vorbis_synthesis_trackonly
functions.description: Parses a packet for tracking/timing without full decode; useful for stream analysis. Exact behavior per libvorbis.
requirements: vb must be initialized and valid for synthesis
op must point to a valid packet

functions.name: vorbis_synthesis_blockin
functions.description: Submits a decoded synthesis block into the DSP state to make PCM available.
requirements: v must be an initialized synthesis DSP state
vb must have been filled by vorbis_synthesis and not yet submitted

functions.name: vorbis_synthesis_pcmout
functions.description: Returns pointers to decoded PCM samples available for reading without advancing the read cursor.
requirements: v must be an initialized synthesis DSP state with pending PCM
pcm must be a valid pointer to receive channel pointer arrays
Do not free or modify returned internal buffers; call vorbis_synthesis_read to advance

functions.name: vorbis_synthesis_lapout
functions.description: Like pcmout but returns PCM with overlap/add considerations suitable for lap processing.
requirements: v must be an initialized synthesis DSP state
pcm must be a valid pointer to receive channel pointer arrays

functions.name: vorbis_synthesis_read
functions.description: Advances the read cursor by samples after consuming data returned by pcmout/lapout.
requirements: v must be an initialized synthesis DSP state
samples must be non-negative and not exceed the amount available from previous pcmout/lapout

functions.name: vorbis_packet_blocksize
functions.description: Returns the block size (window size) indicated by a packet according to the stream setup.
requirements: vi must be initialized/populated by headers
op must point to a valid Vorbis packet

functions.name: vorbis_synthesis_halfrate
functions.description: Enables or disables half-rate decoding for a stream (reduced sample rate decode).
requirements: v must be initialized/populated by headers
flag is 0 to disable, nonzero to enable

functions.name: vorbis_synthesis_halfrate_p
functions.description: Queries whether half-rate decoding is enabled for the given stream setup.
requirements: v must be initialized/populated by headers

functions.name: vorbis_encode_init
functions.signature: extern int vorbis_encode_init(vorbis_info *vi, long channels, long rate, long max_bitrate, long nominal_bitrate, long min_bitrate);
functions.description: One-shot initialization of encoder setup in vi for managed/nominal bitrate modes.
requirements: vi must be initialized with vorbis_info_init before calling
channels and rate specify the input configuration and must be valid (out-of-range is OV_EINVAL)
max_bitrate, nominal_bitrate, min_bitrate: use -1 to indicate unset as documented
On success, proceed with vorbis_analysis_init and header generation; call vorbis_info_clear after encoding

functions.name: vorbis_encode_setup_managed
functions.signature: extern int vorbis_encode_setup_managed(vorbis_info *vi, long channels, long rate, long max_bitrate, long nominal_bitrate, long min_bitrate);
functions.description: Step 1 of 3 for managed bitrate encoder setup; allows later tuning via vorbis_encode_ctl before finalizing with vorbis_encode_setup_init.
requirements: vi must be initialized with vorbis_info_init
channels and rate must be valid
Bitrate parameters: -1 indicates unset per docs
Must call vorbis_encode_setup_init to finalize before encoding; optional vorbis_encode_ctl may be called between setup and init

functions.name: vorbis_encode_setup_vbr
functions.signature: extern int vorbis_encode_setup_vbr(vorbis_info *vi, long channels, long rate, float quality);
functions.description: Step 1 of 3 for variable-bitrate (quality) encoder setup; allows later tuning via vorbis_encode_ctl before finalizing with vorbis_encode_setup_init.
requirements: vi must be initialized with vorbis_info_init
channels and rate must be valid
quality is a float, documented typical range -0.1 to 1.0
Must call vorbis_encode_setup_init to finalize before encoding; optional vorbis_encode_ctl may be called between setup and init

functions.name: vorbis_encode_init_vbr
functions.signature: extern int vorbis_encode_init_vbr(vorbis_info *vi, long channels, long rate, float base_quality);
functions.description: One-shot initialization of encoder setup in vi for VBR (quality-based) mode.
requirements: vi must be initialized with vorbis_info_init
channels and rate must be valid
base_quality documented typical range -0.1 to 1.0
On success, proceed with vorbis_analysis_init and header generation; call vorbis_info_clear after encoding

functions.name: vorbis_encode_setup_init
functions.description: Finalizes the high-level encoding setup previously created by vorbis_encode_setup_managed or vorbis_encode_setup_vbr. No further setup changes allowed afterward.
requirements: vi must be initialized and must have been prepared by vorbis_encode_setup_managed or vorbis_encode_setup_vbr
Do not attempt further vorbis_encode_ctl modifications after successful init
After encoding, clear with vorbis_info_clear

functions.name: vorbis_encode_ctl
functions.description: Generic control interface to query or set encoder parameters using request codes (e.g., OV_ECTL_*). Must be called after setup_managed/setup_vbr and before setup_init for modifications; may also be used for queries.
requirements: vi must be initialized; for modifications, call only between setup_managed/setup_vbr and setup_init
number must be one of the defined OV_ECTL_* codes
arg must point to the structure/type required by the given code; may be NULL where specified (e.g., RATEMANAGE2_SET can disable management with NULL)

functions.name: ov_clear
functions.description: Clears and closes an OggVorbis_File, releasing internal resources and closing the datasource if managed by callbacks.
requirements: vf must have been initialized by ov_open/ov_open_callbacks/ov_fopen/ov_test
After calling, vf is no longer usable until reopened
Behavior of closing depends on callbacks supplied (e.g., NOCLOSE avoids closing)

functions.name: ov_fopen
functions.description: Convenience open routine that opens a file by path and initializes OggVorbis_File using standard stdio callbacks.
requirements: path must be a valid C string path to an existing readable file
vf must be a valid, writable pointer
On success, later call ov_clear to release resources

functions.name: ov_open
functions.description: Initializes OggVorbis_File using an existing stdio FILE* with optional initial buffer for stream data.
requirements: f must be a valid FILE* (seekable recommended unless streaming)
vf must be a valid, writable pointer
initial may be NULL or point to ibytes of initial data; ibytes specifies its length
Prefer ov_open_callbacks on Windows to avoid CRT mismatches, per header note
Call ov_clear when done

functions.name: ov_open_callbacks
functions.signature: extern int ov_open_callbacks(void *datasource, OggVorbis_File *vf, const char *initial, long ibytes, ov_callbacks callbacks);
functions.description: Initializes OggVorbis_File with user-provided I/O callbacks around an arbitrary datasource. Supports unseekable streams if seek_func returns -1.
requirements: datasource must be a valid pointer understood by the provided callbacks
vf must be a valid, writable pointer
callbacks.read_func must be non-NULL; other callbacks may be NULL depending on needs
If the stream is unseekable, seek_func must be NULL or must return -1 for attempts, per docs
initial may be NULL or point to ibytes of initial data
Call ov_clear when done

functions.name: ov_test
functions.description: Partial open that tests a FILE* to determine if it is Vorbis without fully opening/decoding; can be completed with ov_test_open.
requirements: f must be a valid FILE*
vf must be a valid pointer
initial/ibytes semantics as ov_open
Call ov_test_open to finish opening or ov_clear to discard

functions.name: ov_test_callbacks
functions.signature: extern int ov_test_callbacks(void *datasource, OggVorbis_File *vf, const char *initial, long ibytes, ov_callbacks callbacks);
functions.description: Partial open with user callbacks to test a datasource for Vorbis; complete with ov_test_open.
requirements: datasource valid for given callbacks
vf valid pointer
callbacks as per ov_open_callbacks (read_func required)
initial/ibytes optional as documented
Complete with ov_test_open or clear with ov_clear

functions.name: ov_test_open
functions.description: Completes a prior ov_test/ov_test_callbacks and fully opens the OggVorbis_File for decoding.
requirements: vf must have been initialized by ov_test or ov_test_callbacks and be in PARTOPEN state
On success, use other ov_ APIs; on failure, clear state with ov_clear

functions.name: ov_bitrate
functions.description: Returns the nominal bitrate of link i or the entire stream depending on i; exact semantics per libvorbisfile.
requirements: vf must be opened via ov_open/ov_fopen/ov_open_callbacks/ov_test_open
i selects a link; use -1 for the current logical bitstream or per libvorbisfile semantics

functions.name: ov_bitrate_instant
functions.description: Returns an instantaneous bitrate estimate of the currently decoding stream.
requirements: vf must be opened and decoding or have data available

functions.name: ov_streams
functions.description: Returns the number of logical bitstreams (links) within the opened file/stream.
requirements: vf must be opened successfully

functions.name: ov_seekable
functions.description: Returns nonzero if the datasource is seekable, zero if not.
requirements: vf must be opened successfully

functions.name: ov_serialnumber
functions.description: Returns the Ogg stream serial number for link i, or for current link depending on i.
requirements: vf must be opened successfully
i indexes a link; per libvorbisfile semantics

functions.name: ov_raw_total
functions.description: Returns total bytes of compressed data for link i or the entire stream.
requirements: vf must be opened successfully
i selects link or entire stream per API convention

functions.name: ov_pcm_total
functions.description: Returns total PCM samples for link i or the entire stream.
requirements: vf must be opened successfully
i selects link or entire stream per API convention

functions.name: ov_time_total
functions.description: Returns total playback time in seconds for link i or the entire stream.
requirements: vf must be opened successfully
i selects link or entire stream per API convention

functions.name: ov_raw_seek
functions.description: Seeks to a byte offset within the compressed data of a seekable stream.
requirements: vf must be opened and seekable (ov_seekable != 0)
pos must be a valid byte offset within the stream

functions.name: ov_pcm_seek
functions.description: Seeks to an absolute PCM sample position in a seekable stream (sample-accurate).
requirements: vf must be opened and seekable
pos is the target PCM sample position (non-negative, within total)

functions.name: ov_pcm_seek_page
functions.description: Seeks to a PCM position, landing on the nearest page boundary for efficiency.
requirements: vf must be opened and seekable
pos within valid range

functions.name: ov_time_seek
functions.description: Seeks to an absolute playback time (seconds) in a seekable stream (sample-accurate).
requirements: vf must be opened and seekable
pos in seconds within valid total duration

functions.name: ov_time_seek_page
functions.description: Seeks to a playback time (seconds), aligning to the nearest page boundary.
requirements: vf must be opened and seekable
pos within valid duration

functions.name: ov_raw_seek_lap
functions.description: Like ov_raw_seek but performs a lap on the PCM output to avoid artifacts at the seek point.
requirements: vf must be opened and seekable
pos is a valid byte offset

functions.name: ov_pcm_seek_lap
functions.description: Like ov_pcm_seek but laps the PCM output to reduce discontinuities at the seek point.
requirements: vf must be opened and seekable
pos is a valid PCM sample position

functions.name: ov_pcm_seek_page_lap
functions.description: Like ov_pcm_seek_page but with lapping to reduce artifacts.
requirements: vf must be opened and seekable
pos is a valid PCM sample position

functions.name: ov_time_seek_lap
functions.description: Like ov_time_seek but laps the PCM output to reduce artifacts.
requirements: vf must be opened and seekable
pos is a valid time in seconds

functions.name: ov_time_seek_page_lap
functions.description: Like ov_time_seek_page but with lapping to reduce artifacts.
requirements: vf must be opened and seekable
pos is a valid time in seconds

functions.name: ov_raw_tell
functions.description: Returns the current raw (byte) position in the compressed stream.
requirements: vf must be opened successfully

functions.name: ov_pcm_tell
functions.description: Returns the current PCM sample position.
requirements: vf must be opened successfully

functions.name: ov_time_tell
functions.description: Returns the current playback time position in seconds.
requirements: vf must be opened successfully

functions.name: ov_info
functions.description: Returns a pointer to the vorbis_info for a given link or current stream; do not modify or free.
requirements: vf must be opened successfully
link selects which logical bitstream; per API semantics
Returned pointer is owned by vf; do not free or modify; remains valid while vf is open

functions.name: ov_comment
functions.description: Returns a pointer to the vorbis_comment for a given link or current stream; do not modify or free.
requirements: vf must be opened successfully
link selects which logical bitstream; per API semantics
Returned pointer is owned by vf; do not free or modify; remains valid while vf is open

functions.name: ov_read_float
functions.description: Decodes up to samples PCM frames into internal float buffers and returns pointers to per-channel data; does not interleave. Returns number of samples produced or 0 on EOF, negative on error.
requirements: vf must be opened and prepared for decoding
pcm_channels must be a valid pointer to receive channel arrays
samples is the requested number of samples (frames) to return
bitstream may be non-NULL to receive the current logical bitstream index
Consume data by copying; buffers are owned by vf and may be invalidated by subsequent calls

functions.name: ov_read_filter
functions.signature: extern long ov_read_filter(OggVorbis_File *vf,char *buffer,int length, int bigendianp,int word,int sgned,int *bitstream, void (*)(float **pcm,long channels,long samples,void *filter_param),void *filter_param);
functions.description: Decodes audio, applies a user filter callback over float PCM, then writes converted PCM into buffer according to endianness/word size/sign parameters. Returns bytes read, 0 on EOF, or negative on error.
requirements: vf must be opened and prepared for decoding
buffer must be a valid writable buffer of at least length bytes
length is the maximum number of bytes to write
bigendianp specifies endianness (0 little, nonzero big)
word specifies bytes per sample (typically 1 or 2)
sgned specifies signedness (nonzero for signed)
bitstream may be non-NULL to receive current link index
filter must be NULL or a valid function pointer; filter_param passed through

functions.name: ov_read
functions.signature: extern long ov_read(OggVorbis_File *vf,char *buffer,int length, int bigendianp,int word,int sgned,int *bitstream);
functions.description: Decodes audio and writes interleaved PCM into buffer with specified endianness/word size/signedness. Returns number of bytes written, 0 on EOF, or negative on error.
requirements: vf must be opened and prepared for decoding
buffer must be a valid writable buffer of at least length bytes
length is max bytes to write
bigendianp selects endianness (0 little, nonzero big)
word selects bytes per sample (typically 1 or 2)
sgned selects signedness (nonzero signed)
bitstream may be non-NULL to receive current link index

functions.name: ov_crosslap
functions.description: Performs a cross-lap between two opened OggVorbis_File decoders to splice streams smoothly (reduce discontinuities).
requirements: vf1 and vf2 must both be opened and ready for decoding
Streams must be compatible for crossfading/lapping (exact constraints unspecified here)

functions.name: ov_halfrate
functions.description: Enables or disables half-rate decoding for an opened file, reducing output sample rate by half.
requirements: vf must be opened successfully
flag is 0 to disable, nonzero to enable
May affect decoder state; set before decoding for consistent behavior

functions.name: ov_halfrate_p
functions.description: Queries whether half-rate decoding is enabled for an opened file.
requirements: vf must be opened successfully

data_types.description: A NUL-terminated byte sequence suitable for APIs expecting const char*. May contain arbitrary bytes except it must include a terminating NUL for correct C-string semantics. Used for tags, values, and raw comment strings like "TAG=VALUE".

Arbitrary byte buffer interpreted as an Ogg Vorbis packet payload. When valid, it may be one of: identification header, comment header, setup header, or audio data packet, as defined by the Vorbis specification. The buffer is passed via ogg_packet.packet with length ogg_packet.bytes and may be invalid, truncated, or random for fuzzing.

import random
import string
from typing import List

# This generator targets C strings used by vorbis_comment* APIs.
# The fuzzing harness obtains std::string from FUZZ_PARAM_STR() and passes c_str()
# Therefore our buffer should contain one or more NUL-terminated strings that the
# harness can slice out. We will emit a sequence of concatenated NUL-terminated
# C strings representing typical Vorbis comments and tags/values.
#
# Goals:
# - Provide a mix of raw "TAG=VALUE" comments for vorbis_comment_add.
# - Provide standalone tags and values for vorbis_comment_add_tag, including
#   empty value cases (contents may be NULL in harness randomly) and unicode/utf8.
# - Include edge cases: empty tag fallback (harness replaces empty with "X"),
#   very long values, values with '=' and embedded NUL-safe structure as separate strings.
# - Keep total buffer <= 4096 bytes.
# - Deterministic randomness given seed.

MAX_TOTAL = 4096

COMMON_TAGS = [
    "TITLE", "ARTIST", "ALBUM", "TRACKNUMBER", "DATE", "GENRE", "COMMENT",
    "DESCRIPTION", "PERFORMER", "COPYRIGHT", "LICENSE", "ORGANIZATION",
    "LOCATION", "CONTACT", "ISRC", "ALBUMARTIST", "DISCNUMBER", "COMPOSER",
    "ENCODER"
]

UNICODE_SAMPLES = [
    "こんにちは",  # Japanese
    "Привет",      # Russian
    "안녕하세요",     # Korean
    "¡Hola!",     # Spanish punctuation
    "你好",         # Chinese
    "Γειά σου",     # Greek
    "مرحبا",       # Arabic (RTL)
    "😊🎵",        # Emojis
]

ASCII_PUNCT = "-_ .,:;!?'\"/\\()[]{}@#%&+*~|^$"


def _rand_ascii_word(rng: random.Random, min_len=1, max_len=16) -> str:
    n = rng.randint(min_len, max_len)
    alphabet = string.ascii_letters + string.digits + ASCII_PUNCT
    return ''.join(rng.choice(alphabet) for _ in range(n))


def _rand_utf8(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    choice = rng.randint(0, 3)
    if choice == 0:
        return _rand_ascii_word(rng, 0, 32)
    elif choice == 1:
        return rng.choice(UNICODE_SAMPLES)
    else:
        # Build mixed string
        parts = []
        for _ in range(rng.randint(1, 4)):
            if rng.random() < 0.5:
                parts.append(_rand_ascii_word(rng, 0, 12))
            else:
                parts.append(rng.choice(UNICODE_SAMPLES))
        return ' '.join(parts).strip()


def _make_tag(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    if rng.random() < 0.6:
        tag = rng.choice(COMMON_TAGS)
    else:
        # Random uppercase tag without '=' and no NULs
        base = _rand_ascii_word(rng, 1, 12)
        tag = ''.join(ch for ch in base if ch.isalnum())
        if not tag:
            tag = 'X'
        tag = tag.upper()[:24]
    return tag


def _make_value(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # Values can be empty, ASCII, or UTF-8; sometimes long
    roll = rng.random()
    if roll < 0.1:
        return ''
    elif roll < 0.7:
        return _rand_utf8(rng)
    else:
        # Longer text paragraph-like
        words = [_rand_utf8(rng) for _ in range(rng.randint(5, 30))]
        s = ' '.join(words)
        # Clamp length
        if len(s) > 512:
            s = s[:512]
        return s


def _make_raw_comment(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    tag = _make_tag(rng)
    val = _make_value(rng)
    # Occasionally include '=' inside value to exercise parsing behavior (valid by spec)
    if val and rng.random() < 0.2:
        parts = val.split()
        if parts:
            insert_at = rng.randint(0, len(parts))
            parts.insert(insert_at, '=')
            val = ' '.join(parts)
    return f"{tag}={val}"


def _cstr(s: str) -> bytes:
    # Encode as UTF-8 and append NUL terminator
    return s.encode('utf-8', 'strict') + b'\x00'


def _unique(strings: List[str]) -> List[str]:
    seen = set()
    out = []
    for s in strings:
        if s not in seen:
            seen.add(s)
            out.append(s)
    return out


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    chunks: List[bytes] = []

    # Strategy: provide a block with a variety of strings in this order:
    # 1) Several raw TAG=VALUE comments (for vorbis_comment_add)
    # 2) Several tags alone (for vorbis_comment_add_tag tag parameter)
    # 3) Several values alone (for contents parameter when not NULL)
    # 4) Edge cases: minimal '=', empty strings replaced by harness, long values

    # Count planning based on size budget
    target_raw = rng.randint(5, 20)
    target_tags = rng.randint(5, 15)
    target_vals = rng.randint(5, 15)

    raw_comments = _unique([_make_raw_comment(rng) for _ in range(target_raw)])
    tags = _unique([_make_tag(rng) for _ in range(target_tags)])
    values = []
    # Ensure some common values present
    fixed_values = [
        "",  # empty (harness may pass NULL separately)
        "0",
        "1",
        "Yes",
        "No",
        "true",
        "false",
        "2025-12-14",
        "Track 01",
        "1234567890",
    ]
    values.extend(fixed_values)
    values.extend([_make_value(rng) for _ in range(target_vals)])

    # Edge-case raw comments
    edge_raw = [
        "=",                 # empty tag, empty value (harness ensures non-empty but allow)
        "X=",                # non-empty tag, empty value
        "TITLE=",            # explicit empty
        "ARTIST=Unknown",
        "GENRE=Rock/Pop",
        "COMMENT=Line1\\nLine2",
        "DESCRIPTION=Emoji 😊🎵",
    ]

    # Assemble in an order likely to be consumed flexibly by the harness
    ordered_strings: List[str] = []
    ordered_strings.extend(raw_comments[: len(raw_comments)//2])
    ordered_strings.extend(tags)
    ordered_strings.extend(values)
    ordered_strings.extend(edge_raw)
    ordered_strings.extend(raw_comments[len(raw_comments)//2 :])

    # Serialize with NUL terminators, ensuring we do not exceed MAX_TOTAL
    total = 0
    for s in ordered_strings:
        b = _cstr(s)
        if total + len(b) > MAX_TOTAL:
            break
        chunks.append(b)
        total += len(b)

    # Guarantee at least one valid string for safety
    if not chunks:
        chunks.append(_cstr("X="))

    return b''.join(chunks)

import random
import struct
import zlib

# This generator produces valid-ish Vorbis ogg_packet payloads covering:
# - Identification header
# - Comment header (with vendor string and user comments)
# - Setup header (minimal plausible, though not fully spec-valid)
# - Small audio packets (framing bit, mode number, simple floor/residue placeholders)
# The aim is to provide coherent, self-consistent bytes so that decoder paths
# like vorbis_synthesis_idheader and vorbis_synthesis_headerin can often accept them.
# We keep sizes <= 4096 bytes.

# Vorbis header packet format basics:
# - First byte: 0x01 (id), 0x03 (comment), or 0x05 (setup)
# - Followed by the 6-byte ASCII string "vorbis"
# Identification header fields (little-endian):
#   version(32), channels(8), sample_rate(32), bitrate_max(32), bitrate_nom(32), bitrate_min(32),
#   blocksize(8: 4-bit small exp, 4-bit large exp), framing_flag(8==0x01)
# Comment header:
#   vendor_length(32), vendor_string, user_comment_list_length(32), then N comments:
#     length(32), comment bytes; finally framing_flag(8==0x01)
# Setup header is complex; we emit a small placeholder blob after signature to pass header checks
# in some implementations even if later decoding may fail. Many libs accept it at headerin stage
# only if consistent with id header; but fuzz infra will also feed random packets.


def _le32(x: int) -> bytes:
    return struct.pack('<I', x & 0xFFFFFFFF)


def _u8(x: int) -> bytes:
    return struct.pack('B', x & 0xFF)


def _rand_ascii(rng: random.Random, min_len: int, max_len: int) -> bytes:
    n = rng.randint(min_len, max_len)
    # Use printable subset plus some UTF-8 bytes to vary
    alphabet = [
        *(list(range(0x20, 0x7F))),
        0x0A, 0x0D, 0x09,
    ]
    data = bytes(rng.choice(alphabet) for _ in range(n))
    return data


def build_ident_header(rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # Reasonable channels and sample rates
    version = 0
    channels = rng.choice([1, 2, 3, 6])
    rate = rng.choice([8000, 11025, 16000, 22050, 32000, 44100, 48000])
    # Bitrate hints: often -1 for unset, use some plausible combos
    pick = rng.randint(0, 4)
    if pick == 0:
        bmax, bnom, bmin = -1, -1, -1
    elif pick == 1:
        bnom = rng.choice([64000, 96000, 128000, 160000, 192000])
        bmin = int(bnom * 0.7)
        bmax = int(bnom * 1.3)
    elif pick == 2:
        bnom = rng.choice([45000, 75000, 112000])
        bmin = -1
        bmax = -1
    else:
        bmax, bnom, bmin = 256000, 160000, 96000

    # Blocksize exponents: small 64/128/256/512, large 512/1024/2048/4096 with large>=small
    small_exp = rng.choice([6, 7, 8, 9])
    large_exp = rng.choice([max(small_exp, 9), 10, 11, 12])
    blocksize = ((small_exp & 0x0F) | ((large_exp & 0x0F) << 4))

    buf = bytearray()
    buf += b"\x01vorbis"  # packet type + signature
    buf += _le32(version)
    buf += _u8(channels)
    buf += _le32(rate)
    # 32-bit signed little-endian for bitrates
    buf += struct.pack('<i', bmax)
    buf += struct.pack('<i', bnom)
    buf += struct.pack('<i', bmin)
    buf += _u8(blocksize)
    buf += _u8(0x01)  # framing flag
    return bytes(buf)


def build_comment_header(rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    vendor = rng.choice([
        b"Xiph.Org libVorbis I 2023",
        b"AOtuEnc",
        b"ffmpeg libvorbis",
        b"libvorbis 1.3.7",
    ])
    # Add some random tail to vendor
    if rng.random() < 0.5:
        vendor += b" " + _rand_ascii(rng, 0, 12)

    n_comments = rng.randint(0, 5)
    comments = []
    tags = [b"TITLE", b"ARTIST", b"ALBUM", b"DATE", b"GENRE", b"TRACKNUMBER", b"COMMENT"]
    for _ in range(n_comments):
        tag = rng.choice(tags)
        # Some values empty, some with ASCII, some with UTF-8-ish
        val = _rand_ascii(rng, 0, 32)
        entry = tag + b"=" + val
        comments.append(entry)

    buf = bytearray()
    buf += b"\x03vorbis"
    buf += _le32(len(vendor))
    buf += vendor
    buf += _le32(len(comments))
    for c in comments:
        buf += _le32(len(c))
        buf += c
    buf += _u8(0x01)  # framing flag
    return bytes(buf)


def build_setup_header(rng: random.Random, id_header: bytes) -> bytes:
    # A truly valid setup header is complex. We craft a compact, semi-plausible blob that
    # many headerin implementations accept or at least parse partially before rejecting.
    # We keep it small and deterministic-ish.
    # Include some structure plus a checksum-like field to vary content.
    core = bytearray()
    # Minimalistic pseudo-codebook section: not spec-valid but consistent structure
    core += b"CB" + _le32(rng.getrandbits(32))
    core += b"MD" + _u8(rng.randint(0, 3))
    core += b"FL" + _le32(rng.randint(0, 3))
    core += b"RS" + _le32(rng.randint(0, 3))
    core += b"MS" + _u8(rng.randint(0, 1))
    # Append hash of id header to correlate
    core += b"IH" + _le32(zlib.crc32(id_header))
    payload = bytes(core)
    buf = bytearray()
    buf += b"\x05vorbis"
    buf += payload
    return bytes(buf)


def build_audio_packet(rng: random.Random, mode_count: int = 2) -> bytes:
    # Vorbis packets are bit-packed; we simplify by emitting a small LSB-first bitstream:
    # - 1 bit: packet_type=0 (audio)
    # - mode bits: ceil(log2(mode_count))
    # - following arbitrary bytes as payload; we end with random size 10..60 bytes
    # Even if not fully valid, this looks like an audio packet to many paths.
    n_modes = max(1, mode_count)
    mbits = 1
    while (1 << mbits) < n_modes:
        mbits += 1
    # Build first few bits
    # We'll assemble bits into bytes LSB-first
    bits = []
    bits.append(0)  # audio packet flag
    mode = rng.randrange(n_modes)
    for i in range(mbits):
        bits.append((mode >> i) & 1)
    # Add some extra alignment bits
    extra_bits = rng.randint(0, 7)
    for _ in range(extra_bits):
        bits.append(rng.randint(0, 1))
    # Pack bits into bytes
    out = bytearray()
    cur = 0
    nbit = 0
    for b in bits:
        if b:
            cur |= (1 << nbit)
        nbit += 1
        if nbit == 8:
            out.append(cur)
            cur = 0
            nbit = 0
    if nbit:
        out.append(cur)
    # Append some pseudo payload
    payload_len = rng.randint(10, 60)
    out += bytes(rng.getrandbits(8) for _ in range(payload_len))
    return bytes(out)


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    choice = rng.randint(0, 9)

    # Bias toward valid header triplets sometimes to exercise headerin
    if choice in (0, 1):
        idh = build_ident_header(rng)
        comm = build_comment_header(rng)
        setup = build_setup_header(rng, idh)
        # Return exactly one randomly chosen header to feed headerin or idheader paths
        pick = rng.choice([idh, comm, setup])
        return pick[:4096]

    elif choice in (2, 3):
        # Full header triplet concatenated (some stubs may only take one packet; if used as
        # a single packet, idheader will still match on first byte and signature)
        idh = build_ident_header(rng)
        comm = build_comment_header(rng)
        setup = build_setup_header(rng, idh)
        blob = idh + comm + setup
        return blob[:4096]

    elif choice in (4, 5):
        # Identification header specifically (useful for vorbis_synthesis_idheader)
        return build_ident_header(rng)

    elif choice == 6:
        # Comment header with multiple entries
        return build_comment_header(rng)

    elif choice == 7:
        # Setup header placeholder
        idh = build_ident_header(rng)
        return build_setup_header(rng, idh)

    else:
        # Audio packet-like payload; vary mode count
        mode_ct = rng.randint(1, 4)
        return build_audio_packet(rng, mode_ct)[:4096]
